correctness.rationale: The full positive-equilibrium Hopf arc is exactly parameterized by t=F/k in (0,1), with the Jacobian determinant k^2-F^2>0. An explicit invertible time-preserving coordinate change reduces the vector field to dot x=omega y+N, dot y=-omega x+(F/omega)N. Direct quadratic homological elimination gives complex cubic resonance with real part (3F-k)/(8(k-F)) and imaginary part (9F^2+6Fk+5k^2)/(24 omega (k-F)), both reproduced by the included exact SymPy script from the polynomial ODE. The positive imaginary part gives the universal angular slowing of every shrinking periodic orbit relative to its simultaneous linear-focus frequency. The first temporal Fourier amplitude of v-v_eq agrees to first order with the resonant radius, fixing normalization. The derivative of C(t) has the sign of a strictly decreasing quartic divided by a negative denominator, hence exactly one global minimum on the open arc, with both endpoint limits infinite. The generalized-Hopf point uses the established nondegenerate Bautin unfolding for small-cycle existence; the angular coefficient does not vanish there. Independent high-accuracy shooting is corroboration, not proof. Uniformity at t endpoints or global-cycle properties are not claimed.

value.rationale: The amplitude-dependence of *physical* cycle time is a natural kinetic observable, distinct from radial stability and from a period trend under simultaneous feed-rate variation. Determining one explicit coefficient for the full exact Hopf arc, proving it remains positive through the Bautin switch, and identifying its unique sharp algebraic minimizer answer a motivated and non-obvious parameter-wide sensitivity question. It is neither a textbook restatement of Hopf existence nor a numerical isolated parameter sample. The result is intrinsically finite-dimensional and local; no broader publication-sized theorem or general downstream application is claimed.
